evals.prompt: This project already has StyleX wired into the Vite build. Can you migrate src/PriceCard.tsx from Tailwind to StyleX without changing how it renders?
evals.expected_output: Rewrites PriceCard.tsx with the StyleX import and a module-level stylex.create call. Every host element uses stylex.props instead of className. Responsive widths and button states use conditional property values with a default. The text utilities keep both font size and line height. No Tailwind classes remain.
expectations: Adds `import * as stylex from '@stylexjs/stylex'` and defines styles with `stylex.create` at module scope
Every element uses `{...stylex.props(...)}`; no `className` or Tailwind utility strings remain
The responsive width from w-full, md:w-1/2, and lg:w-1/3 becomes a `width` object with a 100% default and media keys at 768px and 1024px
Button hover, focus-visible, and disabled states become value-level backgroundColor conditions with a `default` key
text-sm and text-3xl each produce fontSize and lineHeight
Multi-value shorthands are avoided: border is split into borderWidth/borderStyle/borderColor rather than a single `border` string
Rendered result keeps the colors, spacing, radii, and shadow from the Tailwind original

evals.prompt: Please convert src/Button.tsx to StyleX. It uses cn() from ./lib/utils for variants and a caller className, and it renders a Spinner component. Keep the caller override behavior.
evals.expected_output: Rewrites Button.tsx with stylex.create and stylex.props. The style arguments preserve the original variant and loading conditions, with the caller override last. The public API accepts a StyleX style prop instead of className. Spinner receives that style and applies stylex.props to its own svg host element. animate-spin becomes a stylex.keyframes animation.
expectations: The cn(...) call is replaced by stylex.props(...) with the same last-wins ordering
Primary and secondary variants use a conditional style argument inside stylex.props
The loading conditional becomes a `loading && styles.x` argument
The caller override moves from className to a StyleX style prop and stays last in stylex.props
Spinner receives a style prop and applies stylex.props to its own svg host element
animate-spin becomes stylex.keyframes referenced by animationName
No Tailwind class strings or cn import remain in Button.tsx for the migrated element

evals.prompt: Migrate src/Navbar.tsx to StyleX. The project uses class-based dark mode through `darkMode: 'class'` in tailwind.config.ts. Convert what maps cleanly and report anything that needs a structural change.
evals.expected_output: Converts Navbar.tsx to stylex.create and stylex.props. space-x-6 becomes gap on the flex parent. px-[18px] becomes paddingInline set to 18px. The result reports that group-hover requires React state or a shared variable because StyleX cannot target ancestor state. Class-based dark mode uses defineVars with createTheme, or the summary marks that work as required instead of dropping the styles.
expectations: space-x-6 becomes `gap` on the flex container rather than sibling margins
The arbitrary value px-[18px] becomes paddingInline: '18px'
group-hover:opacity-100 is reported as ancestor-state styling with React state or a shared CSS variable as the alternative
Class-based dark mode uses StyleX theming with defineVars and createTheme, or the summary marks that work as required
text-sm and text-lg keep both fontSize and lineHeight
The final summary explicitly calls out space-x, group-hover, and dark-mode handling so the user can review the design-affecting decisions
